user.t:
Side task (this prompt is your spec). Design 3 distinct, original logo concepts for the company "scoup.ai". It sells a B2B SaaS that audits freight invoices and recovers carrier overcharges (the product is currently called "Freight Recovery"). The name plays on "recoup" (getting money back) and "scoop" (finding what others miss). Audience: logistics and finance managers. Tone: trustworthy, precise, calm, not hype. Must not resemble Coupa, Scoutbee, Scout AI or Scope AI marks; avoid clichés (trucks, globes, dollar signs, robot/brain/sparkle AI icons).

Write ONLY into C:[REDACTED:high_entropy] (create it). Do not touch any repo.

Brand palette: start from the product's existing tokens (read C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-build/web/src/styles/tokens.css — slate neutrals + one teal accent) so the logo fits the app; you may propose one refined accent if needed, with contrast ratios ≥4.5:1 for text use and ≥3:1 for the mark on white and on the dark slate.

For EACH concept (concept-1, -2, -3), hand-written SVG with the lettering drawn as vector PATHS (no <text>, no font dependency, no external refs, no scripts, no raster), viewBox-tight, optimized:
- mark.svg (symbol alone, must read at 16px — test as favicon), wordmark.svg ("scoup.ai", lowercase unless the concept argues otherwise; ".ai" visually subordinate), lockup-horizontal.svg, lockup-stacked.svg, plus mono black and mono white (reversed) versions of the lockup, and favicon.svg.
- Rationale (2-3 sentences), clear-space rule (e.g. = height of the mark's x-unit), minimum sizes, and do/don't.
Also write preview.html: a single self-contained page (inline the SVGs, no external resources) showing the three concepts side by side on white, on dark slate, at favicon size (16/32px), in a mock app header (sidebar logo + "Freight Recovery" product name next to it in the "Freight Recovery by scoup.ai" style), and in a mock marketing nav. Light/dark via prefers-color-scheme with tokens on :root; mobile-friendly.
If a headless browser is available locally (check for playwright/puppeteer in C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-build/node_modules without installing anything), render preview.png and each mark at 16/32/64 px PNG and look at them yourself (Read the PNGs) to verify legibility and optical balance; iterate until the letterforms are clean (consistent stroke widths, correct curves, no kinks). If none is available, say so.
Report: file list, a one-paragraph description of each concept, palette with contrast ratios, and which concept you recommend and why.

resp.t: An early background command was stopped when it hit its time limit: a filesystem-wide `find` I started at the beginning to look for a Playwright install. This changes nothing about the delivered work. I found the headless browser I needed by another route, and all renders, checks and the final report were finished before it was stopped, so I'm not restarting it.

handback.t:
I've designed the three concepts and recommend **Concept 3, "Reconciled s"**. Every SVG and preview.html is written and checked: all 39 SVG files parse as valid XML, and a scan found no `<text>`, no external references or `href`, no scripts and no raster images.

I rendered everything with Chrome's headless browser, which I found already installed in Playwright's browser cache (`~[REDACTED:high_entropy]`). Nothing was installed, and there is no Playwright or Puppeteer package in freight-recovery-build/node_modules. I then looked at the PNGs myself and iterated:
- **Stem caps:** the rounded stem tops in Concept 2 were inset so they no longer rise above the x-height.
- **Concept 3 s:** made wider.
- **Favicons:** snapped to the 16px pixel grid.
- **Mark viewBoxes:** tightened to the artwork.
- **Mobile layout:** two overflow bugs in preview.html fixed.

At 2x the curves render smooth and the stroke widths are consistent. The faceting in my first renders came from Chrome's GPU raster; CPU rendering is clean.

I applied the one-brand decision: the mock app header and marketing nav show the scoup.ai lockup alone. In the app header, "Freight invoice recovery" is a separate line you can remove.

## The three concepts
All three share one hand-drawn geometric lowercase "scoup.ai". Circles, arcs and lines are drawn as stroked paths with a uniform stroke, at three weight settings, with optical overshoot on the round letters. ".ai" is drawn lighter and in a muted slate so it reads as subordinate.

**Concept 1, "Recovered share".** A thick slate ring stands for the invoice total. One teal segment in the upper right is lifted slightly outward: the overcharge pulled out and returned. It reads like a calm finance chart that finance managers already know. The lettering has flat stroke ends. It's legible at 16px, but the segment gets soft there. Main risk: it could be read as a loading spinner or a generic pie-chart icon, so the do/don't rules forbid animating it.

**Concept 2, "The scoop".** An open, round-ended cup holds a single teal point: the scoop that catches what others miss. The full stop in ".ai" is teal too, so the mark and the name share one detail. Round stroke ends make it friendly but not playful. It's the cleanest of the three at 16px. Risks: the U shape is close to a plain "U" or magnet, so it is the least ownable. In the black-only version the point can merge visually with the cup at small sizes.

**Concept 3, "Reconciled s".** An s drawn as two halves that meet exactly at the spine, on a rounded tile: invoice and contract, reconciled. The upper half is white and the lower half teal on a slate-900 tile; on dark backgrounds the tile switches to light. The wordmark's s uses the same construction, so the name echoes the mark. It works as an app icon or avatar out of the box and stays a clear "s" at 16px.

## Palette
These are the existing product tokens unchanged; no new accent was needed. Lettering and ".ai" need at least 4.5:1, the marks at least 3:1.

| Colour | Use | Contrast |
|---|---|---|
| Ink #0f172a | letters and mark on light | 17.85:1 on white |
| Teal #0f766e | accent on light | 5.47:1 on white, 5.23:1 on #f8fafc |
| Muted #64748b | ".ai" on light | 4.76:1 on white |
| Ink (dark) #e2e8f0 | letters and mark on dark slate | 15.19:1 on #0b1220 |
| Teal (dark) #2dd4bf | accent on dark | 10.06:1 on #0b1220, 9.59:1 on the #0f172a tile |
| Muted (dark) #8b9ab0 | ".ai" on dark | 6.55:1 on #0b1220 |

On Concept 3's light tile (#e2e8f0): #0f172a is 14.48:1 and #0f766e is 4.44:1, which clears the 3:1 the mark needs. Two pairs fail and are avoided:
- #0f766e on dark slate is only 3.42:1, so dark backgrounds always switch to #2dd4bf.
- The dark tile on dark slate is 1.05:1, which is why the tile turns light on dark backgrounds.

## Rules (shown per concept in preview.html)
- **Clear space:** x = the x-height of the wordmark (the height of the "o"). Keep 1x on all sides of a lockup, and 0.25 × mark height around the mark alone.
- **Minimum sizes:**
  - Horizontal lockup: 20px tall (about 100–105px wide) on screen, 6mm in print.
  - Stacked lockup: 48px tall.
  - Mark: favicon.svg from 16–24px, mark.svg from 24px up.
- **Do/don't:** per concept. For example: don't close the gap or animate Concept 1 as a spinner; don't add dots to Concept 2; don't offset the two halves of Concept 3 or put its dark tile on dark slate.

## Recommendation
Go with Concept 3. It is the most ownable mark and the most directly tied to what the product does (matching invoices against contracts). It is also the only one that keeps the name in the icon: the tile still reads "s" at 16px and works as an app icon or avatar. It sits naturally with the slate and teal UI, and its geometry clearly differs from Coupa, Scoutbee, Scout AI and Scope AI, with no clichés. Concept 2 is the strongest runner-up for pure small-size legibility.

## Before production
- **Stroked artwork:** the lettering is drawn as stroked paths. Before a final release, convert the strokes to outlines and merge the overlaps in a vector editor; this also removes a faint anti-aliasing seam visible at very large sizes where the p and a bowls meet their stems.
- **Concept 3 mono files:** they use an internal mask (`url(#…)`, no external reference).
- **Favicons:** Concepts 1 and 2 switch colours for dark browser themes using a small CSS media query (no script); this was checked in a dark-mode render.
- **Trademark check:** run a formal trademark search before adopting any of these.

## Files
Everything is in `C:[REDACTED:high_entropy]`:
- **preview.html** – the self-contained comparison page.
- **concept-1/, concept-2/, concept-3/** – 13 SVGs each:
  - mark.svg, mark-on-dark.svg
  - wordmark.svg, wordmark-on-dark.svg
  - lockup-horizontal.svg, lockup-horizontal-on-dark.svg
  - lockup-stacked.svg, lockup-stacked-on-dark.svg
  - lockup-horizontal-mono-black.svg, lockup-horizontal-mono-white.svg
  - lockup-stacked-mono-black.svg, lockup-stacked-mono-white.svg
  - favicon.svg (grid-snapped)
- **renders/**:
  - `concept-{1,2,3}-{mark,favicon}-{16,32,64}.png`
  - marks-sizes-zoomed.png
  - preview.png, preview-dark.png, preview-mobile.png
  - wordmark-proof-2x.png
- **_src/** – gen.py, which builds every SVG and preview.html from the geometry (`python _src/gen.py`), plus proof.py, shot.sh and sizes.sh for the renders.

No repository was touched.
